name: final_stressed_f
summary: Final-stressed (incl. monosyllabic) F mostly adopt -en-, a zero linker or an -s-. It is possible that there is a tendency to choose by singular/plural meaning: if the second constituent forces the first constituent to take a collective or plural meaning, -en- is more likely, otherwise mostly a zero linker or -s- is chosen depending on further constraints.

evidence_pro.summary: One-syllable F sometimes adopt -en-, sometimes a zero linker. It is possible that there is a tendency to choose by singular/plural meaning.
-(e)n- sometimes has a plural meaning (especially after weak F) [1].

-en- can be added to monosyllabic or polysyllabic final-stressed weak F only when the plural interpretation is allowed, with a very few counterexamples. If the plural reading is inadequate, another linking element, mostly -s- or zero, has to be chosen.
F not ending in -e [1] do not usually attach -en-; if there is a singular interpretation, they attach a zero linker.
-(e)n- exhibits a very weak positive effect on plural reading (with non-significant p-value) [2].

footnotes.2: This finding concerning plural interpretability of -(e)n- is not very reliable. -(e)n- may occur after different classes of nouns, and the study indeed included occurrences of -(e)n- after nouns from these different classes. All the occurrences were analyzed altogether disregarding the class of the noun. However, as literature points out, these different classes may have different predispositions towards plural interpretability. Thus for example, the tendency of a plural reading of -(e)n- was pointed out by a few papers for F with a stress on the last syllable (incl. monosyllabic F), which is not the case for trochaic F or weak masculines. Thus, making a single conclusion about all occurrences from different classes adopting -(e)n- may be misleading since strong effect of one class may be wiped out by the absence of the same effect for the others. However, since even with this averaging over the classes, the overall effect is positive (even if weakly), we include this finding in the evidence, assuming the effect of -(e)n- after F with a stress on the last syllable (incl. monosyllabic F) was most probably positive as well.

name: schwa
summary: Nouns ending in schwa regularly adopt -n- if the schwa is not a suffix, this is the only class of words that can attach this linker. If the schwa is a suffix of a deadjective F, -n- and zero linkers are about equally possible. Deverbal F with the schwa suffix mostly attach a zero linker but can attach an -n- when the first constituent has a plural reading.

evidence_pro.summary: F ending in schwa (they are already two-syllabic) regularly adopt -n-.
F ending in schwa adopt -n- if schwa is not a suffix, otherwise a zero linker.
F ending in schwa adopt -n- productively.
The claim that F ending in schwa always attach a zero linker is not supported by the empirical data, but it should be marked as a tendency [1].
-n- occurs only after schwa, and most of the words ending with a schwa adopt it.
F ending in schwa will almost always attach an -n- with a very few exceptions [2].

Nouns (especially weak F) ending in schwa mostly adopt -n-. However, deadjective F ending in a schwa suffix have a zero linker or -n- in about the same number of cases. Deverbative F ending in schwa suffix  mostly have a zero linker; they can attach an -n- though when the first constituent has a plural reading. [3, 4]
F ending in schwa virtually always occur with -n-.

footnotes.1: The counterexample there is a deadjective F: tiefe_+n_meter, which is in line with the overall constraint.
footnotes.2: The exception given there is kohle_berg_werk; a variant kohle_+n_berg_werk coexists. Let's consider further counterexample kohle_filter provided here without a coexisting *kohle_+n_filter. Both kohle_berg_werk and kohle_filter can be accounted for if we assume the constraint `tech_term` is stronger than `schwa_f` and thus -- since these are technical terms -- it blocks the application of `schwa_f` in these cases.
footnotes.3: A further claim was made in the paper: 'Finally, further F ending in schwa can adopt an -n- if they denote a concrete countable, even if no plural meaning occurs'. However, these cases simply fall into the cases of F ending in a non-suffix schwa and are only a subset thereof.
footnotes.4: Mixed and irregular M and N ending in schwa also fall here: 'Auge', 'Interesse' can be handled assuming `schwa` > `mixed_mn`. However, many of further examples are eventually overtaken by other constraints: 'Name', 'Glaube'. etc. will be governed by `ens` (assuming `ens` > `schwa`); 'Ende' mostly removes the schwa and is thus not considered in this iteration; 'Gebäude' will be governed by `null_plural` (assuming `null_plural` > `schwa`).

name: copula
summary: Copulative compounds regularly attach a zero linker.

evidence_pro.summary: The probability of a linking element to appear decreases as the compound type becomes closer to syntax: determinative compounds adopt explicit linkers non-systematically; copulative compounds with additive relations can adopt explicit linkers, but less frequently; copulative compounds with appositive relations systematically adopt a zero linker. [1]
Copulative compounds do not attach explicit linkers.
Copulative compounds always have a zero linker. In particular, weak M and F ending with suffix -in always adopt -en- unless they are copulative, in which case they have a zero linker. [2]

footnotes.1: The author defines two different types of copulative compounds: with additive relations and with appositive relations. However, this notation is not conventional. What the author calls 'copulative compounds with additive relations' are not defined as copulative compounds in most of the literature, while what the author calls 'copulative compounds with appositive relations' are what is defined "usual" copulative compounds. Thus, in our terms this finding can be summarized as 'non-copulative compounds adopt explicit linkers non-systematically, while copulative compounds systematically adopt a zero linker'.

name: final_full_v

evidence_pro.summary: After a full vowel, a zero linker always appears.
Nouns ending in a full vowel occur with a zero linker.

footnotes.1: The given counterexample uhu_+s_nest could not be verified. In DeReKo, there are only a few occurrences, and all of them are web pages of the site www.uhusnest.de/. name: tech_term
summary: In technical terminology (economics, law, medicine, etc.), compounds are often missing a linking element (even in cases where it would be obligatory in non-technical context).

evidence_pro.summary: In technical terminology (economics, law, etc.), a linking element is often missing (even in cases where it would be obligatory in comparable instances).
If 'Herz' is used in a medical context, it adopts a zero linker. [1]
In compounds that have a doubful -s- and that are used both in common and specialized language, technical terms usually omit the -s- while the common language keeps it.

footnotes.1: This finding is provided as an example of the constraint.

name: null_plural
summary: Derivatives forming the plural with a zero ending -- especially with suffixes -er, -ler, -ner, -el, -sel, -chen, -lein -- attach a zero linking element regularly. Derivatives with suffix -en also attach a zero linker with a few exceptions unless they are a deverbative, in which case they mostly attach -s-. Simplex M and N, as well as any F forming the plural with a zero ending attach a zero linker in majority of cases.

evidence_pro.summary: Derivatives forming the plural with a zero ending -- especially with suffixes -er, -ler, -ner, -el, -sel, -chen, -lein -- attach a zero linking element regularly. Derivatives with suffix -en also attach a zero linker unless they are a deverbative, in which case they mostly attach -s- [1]. Simplex M and N forming the plural with a zero ending attach a zero linker in 90% of cases. F forming the plural with a zero ending attach a zero linker in 85% of cases.

footnotes.1: For more info on deverbatives see `deverba_en`.

evidence_pro.summary: Compounds with the second constituents 'Mann', 'Frau', 'Leute', 'Tochter', 'Gattin', 'Witwe' can insert -s- or -es-, if the compound designates a person, even when the first constituent would otherwise attach a zero linker.

name: mixed_mn
summary: Mixed M and N can attach -s-, -(e)n-, or a zero linker. -(e)n- may be associated with a plural meaning (with counterexamples).

Strong and mixed M and N often (but surely not always) adopt -s- [2].

name: e_umlaut_plural
summary: Nouns forming the plural with an -e ending and an umlaut mostly have a zero linker. In case of plural or collective meaning they may also non-regularly attach -e- with an umlaut, and this is the only class of words that can attach this linker.

evidence_pro.summary: =e= occurs in some [1] e=plural nouns.
e=plural nouns regularly have a zero linker with a few exceptions.
In compounds with =e=, plural interpretation occurs in most cases.
=e= exhibits moderate effect on plural reading.

name: e_plural
summary: Nouns forming the plural with an -e ending mostly have a zero linker. In case of plural or collective meaning, as well as if it is a monosyllabic noun designating an animal, it may also non-regularly attach -e-, and this is the only class of words that can attach this linker.

evidence_pro.summary: A larger group where -e- occurs is animal designations, but certainly not with all of them.
-e- is always paradigmatic and occurs only after nouns with stressed last syllable [1].
There is an observable tendency to insert -e- after nouns designating animals with many counterexamples.
-e- is always paradigmatic. It occurs most frequently and even partly productively after monosyllabic nouns denoting animals.
e-plural nouns rarely have explicit linkers. -e- is always paradigmatic, occurs mostly after symplexes and never after loanwords, and it mostly signalized a plural or collective meaning.
-e- exhibits insignificant effect on plural reading [2].

footnotes.1: The last claim explains why nouns like 'Teppich' do not attach -e- (teppich_boden).
footnotes.2: This finding concerning plural interpretability of -e- is not very reliable. Most of the entries in the dataset were nouns designating animals -- that, as pointed out in the literature, tendentially attach -e- with no respect to the plural meaning. Furthermore, the sample contained noise such as 'Arzt' which is a e=plural noun. Thus, making a single conclusion about all occurrences from different classes adopting -e- may be misleading since strong effect of one class may be wiped out by the absence of the same effect for the others. However, since even with this averaging over the classes, the overall effect is positive (even if weakly), we include this finding in the evidence, assuming the effect of -e- after non-animal designations was most probably positive as well.

name: sonority_s
summary: The probability of -s- decreases with increasing sonority of the final segment of the first constituent: it is more frequent after plosives, infrequent after nasals and liquids, and it never occurs after a full vowel.

evidence_pro.summary: -s- is impossible with nouns ending in a full vowel.
After a full vowel, a zero linker always appears.
In simpices, -s- occurs more often after plosives, much rarer after nasals and liquids. Furthermore, -s- never occurs after a full vowel [1].

The probability of -s- decreases with increasing sonority of the final segment of the first constituent: it occurs after plosives in about 15-20% and after nasals and liquids in only about 1.8-4.7% of cases, and it never occurs after a full vowel.
Nouns ending in a full vowel never have -s-.
-s- never occurs after a full vowel except for in uhu_+s_nest [2].

Claim about 148 Google searches 'Uhusnest' in 2003 provided in the paper could not be verified either. However, we include this counterexample here assuming the authors had reasons to provide it.

name: er_plural
summary: Nouns forming the plural with an -er with or without an umlaut (these are mostly N and some M, mostly simplices and never loanwords) mostly attach both a zero linker and =er= in different cases, and this is the only class of words that can attach the latter. =er= is more probable (with counterexamples) when a plural meaning is present, in which case these nouns will indicate concrete, countable entities. When having a mass meaning, these nouns tend (with counterexamples) to attach a zero linker. For person and animal designations though, =er= is not necessarily associated with a plural meaning. Another linkers can also be rarely adopted by these nouns.

evidence_pro.summary: =er= occurs only in er=plural nouns. These nouns tend to choose =er= when a plural meaning is present, otherwise a zero linker or another linker, except for person and animal designations, for which =er= is not necessarily associated with a plural meaning.
=er= is always paradigmatic and is found in a few er-plural M and N. [1]
=er= is always paradigmatic.

=er= is always paradigmatic and is often associated with plural meaning, with many counterexamples. When attaching =er=, these nouns often indicate concrete, countable entities, while when having a mass meaning, they tend to attach a zero linker.

Most er-plural nouns attach both =er= and a zero linker in different cases, often depending on plural interpretation (80% singular meaning cases have a zero linker). =er= is always paradigmatic and attaches mostly to N and to some M, mostly simplexes, no loanwords. [2]
=er= with no umlauting exhibits moderate, and =er= with umlauting exhibits significantly strong effect on plural reading.

footnotes.1: [kürschner_2010:18] also mentions: '-er- occurs only after nouns with the stressed last syllable'; however, to the best of our knowledge, this always holds for er-plural nouns and, hence, for the nouns in question since =er= is always paradigmatic.
footnotes.2: Even though not explicitly stated, counterexamples for the plural meaning given in [ortner_müller-bollhagen_1991:98] confirm the hypothesis from [eisenberg_2013:229] that for person and animal designations, =er= is not necessarily associated with a plural meaning: huhn_+=er_keule, kind_+=er_jacke, rind_+=er_brust.
